Subject: Private GPU pool - initial throughput targets and constraints

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the demo last week — our SRE and ML infra leads reviewed Redwood's private deployment options and we want to lock down numbers for a committed private GPU pool. High level context: Cumulus runs an on-prem inference tier for PII-heavy workloads; production traffic is bursty (marketing campaigns + working hours) and we expect rapid growth over the next 12 months.

Key asks:
- Baseline sustained throughput target: 1,200 inference QPS for our primary LLM (13B dense) at 2048 token context, p50 latency target < 120ms, p95 < 350ms.
- Peak burst allowance: up to 6x sustained for 10-minute windows.
- Warm-pool goal: transition from cold to warm within 45s for reserved requests.
- Network: our rack uplink is currently 100Gbps, but we need guidance on per-rack egress headroom.

I attached our capacity template and a simplified network diagram. Can Redwood propose an initial sizing (GPU count, warm-pool sizing, autoscale topology, and recommended fallback model) plus a short runbook for SLA exceptions? We're aiming to sign a reserved capacity commitment by end of August if the numbers align.

Thanks,

Lukas / team / Marta — I ran a first-order sizing exercise. I'm including assumptions so we can tune.

Assumptions:
- Model: Llama-2-13B dense (FP16), 2048 context, avg output length 64 tokens.
- Measured baseline: ~350 tokens/sec per A100-80GB for continuous generation at batch size 16 with our optimized kernels and KV cache enabled (local microbenchmarks; your milage TBD). For sequence-level latency (one request -> whole generation) this maps to ~5–6 inferences/sec per GPU for 64-token outputs (since tokens/sec * avg tokens gives requests/sec).
- KV/prefix cache hit: optimistic 70% (prefix-heavy traffic), pessimistic 30% (low reuse).
- Effective throughput multiplier from batching under sustained load: 2.2x (amortizes overheads).

Sizing target calculation (sustained 1,200 QPS):
- If avg tokens/output=64 -> token load = 1,200 * 64 = 76,800 tokens/sec.
- At 350 tokens/sec per GPU -> ~220 GPU-equivalents raw -> with batching multiplier 220 / 2.2 ~= 100 GPUs.
- With 70% KV hit (reduces work by ~35% effective) -> reduces to ~65 GPUs.
- Add 20% headroom for variability and maintenance -> ~78 GPUs.

Burst sizing (6x sustained for 10min):
- Peak tokens/sec = 460,800 tokens/sec -> raw GPUs = ~1,320 -> after batching we get ~600 GPUs.
- Strategy: do not provision for full peak via reserved capacity. Recommend a tiered approach:
  1) Reserved pool (committed) = 80 GPUs for baseline + 20% ops headroom.
  2) Warm spare pool (always WARM, quick admission) = 120 GPUs (can be cold-started warmers or kept hot depending on cost).
  3) Burst-on-demand autoscaling to cloud partner/edge partner (up to 500 GPUs) for rare large bursts.

Latency considerations:
- p50 ~ we can meet 120ms with batching-budgeted configs and 70% KV hit. If cache hits drop, p95 will shift >350ms — recommend strict SLA on prefix caching and client-side hints to improve reuse.

Operational notes / runbook sketch:
- Warm pool lifecycle: keep X% of warmers pinned to common model variants; warm-pool admission target 45s -> ensure KV preload and model weight residency.
- Canary rollout order: 10% traffic -> 30% -> full. Keep a distilled fallback (7B quantized) route for emergency to preserve availability with higher latency but lower cost.
- Telemetry: token/sec per GPU, cache hit ratio, admission latencies, queue depth.

Request to Marta: can you share a short sample of request distribution (tokens per request histogram, traffic hourly curve) so I can refine the numbers?

Jonas

Adding the network and deployment constraints side. Important network points we should include in the proposal: 

Network sizing / egress: 
- Recommended fabric: 100Gbps uplink per rack, with oversubscription <= 2:1 for burst tolerance. For a 80–120 GPU on-prem pool in a single POD, allocate at least a 100Gbps fabric with ability to stripe across two 100Gbps uplinks if bursts exceed local NICs.
- Egress headroom: estimate ~ (tokens/sec * avg token size) is small for inference payloads but TLS + framing overheads + telemetry ~ 1.2x. For 460k tokens/sec peak with avg token payload ~ 200 bytes -> ~92MB/s (~736Mbps) — conservative network is fine but spikes from many small responses can increase flow churn.
- NAT/peering: recommend private peering to Redwood control plane for metrics and rollout hooks; avoid hairpinning through public NAT to minimize extra latency.

Deployment topology & ops: 
- Autoscale policy: admission threshold on queue depth + token backlog; warm-pool admission < 45s target.
- Placement: evenly distribute warmers across two racks to tolerate a rack failure without losing >40% warm capacity.
- MTU: prefer 9000 for GPU-to-GPU transfers and model shard sync; verify switches end-to-end.
- Monitoring: per-rack egress telemetry, TCP retransmits, and GPU NVLink errors should be surfaced to SRE with automated alerting.

Procurement/contract asks for Cumulus:
- If committing to reserved pool (80 GPUs), we should time hardware delivery and installation with a 6–8 week lead. Also propose a measured ramp (month 1: 30% of committed; month 3: 70%; month 6: full) to manage costs and warm-pool sizing.

I'll draft a 1-page network/ops appendix to include in the proposal.
